evidence.claim: NEDA said the Marcos administration's 8-point socioeconomic agenda would address short-term inflation and shock vulnerability, and longer-term job creation, infrastructure, logistics, energy, digitalization, regulation, and governance.
evidence.title: NEDA to flesh out development agenda for addressing constraints to inclusive growth
evidence.excerpt: NEDA said the Marcos administration's 8-point socioeconomic agenda would address short-term inflation and shock vulnerability, and longer-term job creation, infrastructure, logistics, energy, digitalization, regulation, and governance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official release quoting NEDA's implementation agenda and priorities.
contrary_evidence: It is an agenda statement, not implementation.
The source is official and promotional.

evidence.claim: Marcos's economic managers said the 8-point socioeconomic agenda aimed to cut poverty to 9 percent by the end of the six-year term and raise the Philippines to upper-middle-income status by 2028.
evidence.title: PH socioeconomic agenda presented at IMF, World Bank meeting
evidence.excerpt: Marcos's economic managers said the 8-point socioeconomic agenda aimed to cut poverty to 9 percent by the end of the six-year term and raise the Philippines to upper-middle-income status by 2028.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and agenda bullet list
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated report on official targets announced by the administration.
contrary_evidence: Aspirational target, not observed outcome.
The source is a government newswire.

evidence.claim: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that his administration would fight food-price spikes by increasing production and supporting consumers' purchasing power.
evidence.title: Marcos relays food production agenda in 1st SONA
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that his administration would fight food-price spikes by increasing production and supporting consumers' purchasing power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential directive within the target year, reported on an official agency page.
contrary_evidence: The source is self-reporting and policy intent, not implementation.
The food-price problem was partly inherited and global.

evidence.claim: The Marcos administration's first approved appropriations law increased funding for education, agriculture for food security, health, labor and employment, tourism, public works, and energy.
evidence.title: Senate approves 2023 national budget on third reading
evidence.excerpt: The Marcos administration's first approved appropriations law increased funding for education, agriculture for food security, health, labor and employment, tourism, public works, and energy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific budget allocation with executive attribution and concrete sectoral priorities.
evidence.period_fit: Passed in 2022 as the first budget under Marcos for FY2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the administration level; implementation follows later.
contrary_evidence: Budget approval does not prove spending quality or execution.
Some increases mainly continue existing programs.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said poverty reduction gains were substantial but inequality remained high, with the top 1 percent capturing 17 percent of national income and the bottom 50 percent receiving only 14 percent.
evidence.title: PHILIPPINES: Reducing Inequality Key to Becoming a Middle-Class Society Free of Poverty
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said poverty reduction gains were substantial but inequality remained high, with the top 1 percent capturing 17 percent of national income and the bottom 50 percent receiving only 14 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent distributional evidence with concrete shares.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 distributional context for Marcos's first months.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited baseline and structural conditions; useful as context for the trajectory the administration inherited.
contrary_evidence: The report also credits sustained growth, education, jobs, and social assistance for earlier poverty reduction.
The data are not a direct measure of Marcos-specific 2022 outcomes.

evidence.claim: PSA said StatDev 2022 showed the Philippines made progress on some development goals, with only four of 15 sectoral chapters at average performance and six of nine core indicators meeting targets.
evidence.title: PSA releases the 2022 Statistical Indicators on Philippine Development
evidence.excerpt: PSA said StatDev 2022 showed the Philippines made progress on some development goals, with only four of 15 sectoral chapters at average performance and six of nine core indicators meeting targets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistical synthesis with year-specific targets and outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mixed: combines inherited conditions and Marcos-year implementation; not a direct causal estimate.
contrary_evidence: The same summary says many indicators were still off track.
It is an aggregate planning metric, not a ruler-specific causal estimate.

evidence.claim: The DOH launched PinasLakas on July 26, 2022 to intensify COVID-19 vaccination in Marcos's first 100 days, targeting 90 percent of senior citizens and 50 percent booster coverage for eligible Filipinos.
evidence.title: PinasLakas vaccination launch
evidence.excerpt: The DOH launched PinasLakas on July 26, 2022 to intensify COVID-19 vaccination in Marcos's first 100 days, targeting 90 percent of senior citizens and 50 percent booster coverage for eligible Filipinos.
evidence.source_locator: news release excerpt in search result
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official report of a dated public-health campaign with explicit targets and presidential linkage.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct administration-level attribution; the campaign was implemented by DOH under the Marcos administration.
contrary_evidence: This is a rollout target, not proof of final health outcomes.
Operational delivery still depended on DOH and local partners.

evidence.claim: The DOH said PinasLakas raised full vaccination to 93.81 percent and first-booster coverage to 25.62 percent by October 6, 2022, including 3,433,713 boosted eligible individuals and 45,255 boosted senior citizens.
evidence.title: DOH achieves major strides in fight vs COVID-19, strengthens PH healthcare system
evidence.excerpt: The DOH said PinasLakas raised full vaccination to 93.81 percent and first-booster coverage to 25.62 percent by October 6, 2022, including 3,433,713 boosted eligible individuals and 45,255 boosted senior citizens.
evidence.source_locator: campaign results paragraph in search snippet
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government report with concrete coverage figures and a dated checkpoint.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful: this was a Marcos-directed public-health push executed through DOH.
contrary_evidence: The gains occurred in an inherited pandemic-response system.
The article is an institutional progress report, not an independent evaluation.

evidence.claim: DSWD said updated AICS guidelines expedited aid by simplifying intake and eligibility forms, shortening procedures, and increasing beneficiaries served.
evidence.title: Request for assistance under AICS now easier for clients
evidence.publisher: Department of Social Welfare and Development
evidence.excerpt: DSWD said updated AICS guidelines expedited aid by simplifying intake and eligibility forms, shortening procedures, and increasing beneficiaries served.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 agency announcement with specific procedural changes and implementation effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Administration-level attribution is partial; the reform was implemented by DSWD under Secretary Tulfo, within the Marcos administration.
contrary_evidence: This is an implementation reform, not a measured welfare outcome.
The article attributes the directive to the secretary rather than Marcos personally.

evidence.claim: DSWD said Memorandum Circular No. 19 of 2022 institutionalized WiSUPPORT as a regular program and flagship mental-health intervention for children, PWDs, seniors, OFWs in distress, women in difficult circumstances, first responders, caregivers, and others in distress.
evidence.title: DSWD, partners call for stronger mental health initiatives in 30th National Children’s Month Celebration
evidence.publisher: Department of Social Welfare and Development
evidence.excerpt: DSWD said Memorandum Circular No. 19 of 2022 institutionalized WiSUPPORT as a regular program and flagship mental-health intervention for children, PWDs, seniors, OFWs in distress, women in difficult circumstances, first responders, caregivers, and others in distress.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated agency announcement with a precise program definition and target groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Administration-level attribution; the program sits within the Marcos-era DSWD, not a personal presidential directive.
contrary_evidence: Program design does not prove reach or quality in all cases.
The page focuses on advocacy, not audited outcomes.

evidence.claim: DepEd issued School Year 2022-2023 guidelines committing to the resumption of five-day in-person classes, with ALS beginning at school opening and BEDP 2030 and the Learning Recovery and Continuity Plan guiding implementation.
evidence.title: DepEd releases guidelines for School Year 2022-2023
evidence.excerpt: DepEd issued School Year 2022-2023 guidelines committing to the resumption of five-day in-person classes, with ALS beginning at school opening and BEDP 2030 and the Learning Recovery and Continuity Plan guiding implementation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated official policy with explicit school-opening and ALS provisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Administration-level attribution is partial; DepEd led the measure under VP-Secretary Sara Duterte within the Marcos administration.
contrary_evidence: The policy was executed by DepEd rather than Marcos personally.
It reflects recovery from pandemic disruption more than a new social-welfare architecture.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said millions of children returned to school on August 22, 2022, warned that learning poverty hit vulnerable children with disabilities and those in disaster or conflict zones hardest, and noted support for WASH and rapid literacy assessments.
evidence.title: UNICEF celebrates learners’ first day back in school
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said millions of children returned to school on August 22, 2022, warned that learning poverty hit vulnerable children with disabilities and those in disaster or conflict zones hardest, and noted support for WASH and rapid literacy assessments.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct UNICEF press release with precise date, policy context, and vulnerable-group framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; this documents the education environment and partner-supported recovery under the Marcos administration rather than a single presidential order.
contrary_evidence: UNICEF is describing system recovery, not assigning credit to Marcos personally.
The learning crisis predated the administration.

evidence.claim: UNICEF and DepEd launched the ALS 2.0 ICT Strategic Plan and Research Agenda to help out-of-school youth and adults access flexible pathways to complete basic education and improve their lives.
evidence.title: DepEd, UNICEF strengthen Alternative Learning System toward quality, relevant second chance basic education
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF and DepEd launched the ALS 2.0 ICT Strategic Plan and Research Agenda to help out-of-school youth and adults access flexible pathways to complete basic education and improve their lives.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct joint press release with explicit reform content and target population.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect administration-level attribution; DepEd led the policy, and it fits Marcos-era education recovery.
contrary_evidence: The measure was led by DepEd and UNICEF, not directly by Marcos.
It is a program-strengthening step, not a proven outcome measure.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said its Philippines work from April to September 2022 included accelerating learning recovery, bringing child protection services closer through TeleCPUs, and building a more equitable world through digital public goods.
evidence.title: For every child, results - Issue 3
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said its Philippines work from April to September 2022 included accelerating learning recovery, bringing child protection services closer through TeleCPUs, and building a more equitable world through digital public goods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Bulletin-style report with a dated coverage window and concrete program themes, though not a ruler-specific audit.
evidence.period_fit: April to September 2022 coverage within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; useful as evidence of the welfare service environment under the Marcos administration, not of direct presidential authorship.
contrary_evidence: This is a UNICEF summary, not a Marcos performance evaluation.
It aggregates partner work across multiple actors.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said health workers in Southern Leyte were better able to address malnutrition after support, and the province had recorded 160 severe acute malnutrition cases and 565 moderate acute malnutrition cases in the first quarter.
evidence.title: For every child, nutrition even in emergency situations
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said health workers in Southern Leyte were better able to address malnutrition after support, and the province had recorded 160 severe acute malnutrition cases and 565 moderate acute malnutrition cases in the first quarter.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct story with named local figures and a defined disaster-recovery context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; this is crisis-response context rather than a Marcos-issued directive, but it reflects the social need the administration faced.
contrary_evidence: The article centers on UNICEF and local health workers, not Marcos.
It shows continuing need as much as program response.

evidence.claim: UNICEF described a child with cerebral palsy in Southern Leyte whose care and nutrition were disrupted by Typhoon Odette, damaged housing, and blocked roads, illustrating how disasters worsened access for vulnerable families.
evidence.title: Supporting Most Vulnerable Children to Fight Malnutrition in Southern Leyte
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF described a child with cerebral palsy in Southern Leyte whose care and nutrition were disrupted by Typhoon Odette, damaged housing, and blocked roads, illustrating how disasters worsened access for vulnerable families.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct case-based reporting with a clear vulnerability and disaster-access narrative.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect crisis context; not a direct Marcos action, but relevant to the vulnerability baseline his administration inherited and faced.
contrary_evidence: This is a humanitarian case study, not a ruler-attribution finding.
The article does not test government program effectiveness directly.

evidence.claim: DHSUD said ESAP would be improved under Marcos directives with better coordination with DSWD, providing calamity-affected families emergency cash assistance or construction materials to repair damaged houses.
evidence.title: DHSUD one with Marcos admin in boosting disaster response ops
evidence.excerpt: DHSUD said ESAP would be improved under Marcos directives with better coordination with DSWD, providing calamity-affected families emergency cash assistance or construction materials to repair damaged houses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire reporting a specific presidential directive and program change, with direct policy detail.
contrary_evidence: The delivery mechanism remained DHSUD/DSWD-led rather than personally presidential.
This is shelter relief, not a full welfare-system evaluation.

evidence.claim: NEDA said the national ID system would strengthen monitoring for social protection distribution, and the government was using fuel subsidies for drivers, farmers, and fisherfolk to cushion price shocks.
evidence.title: Marcos admin ensures continued economic recovery from pandemic
evidence.excerpt: NEDA said the national ID system would strengthen monitoring for social protection distribution, and the government was using fuel subsidies for drivers, farmers, and fisherfolk to cushion price shocks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official-government newswire with a detailed, dated report on administration measures and implementation path.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct administration-level attribution, though several measures were inherited or jointly managed across agencies.
contrary_evidence: The report frames measures as recovery management, not durable welfare transformation.
Some components, such as the national ID, were already in motion before Marcos.

evidence.claim: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that the administration would raise production to counter food-price spikes and support purchasing power.
evidence.title: Marcos relays food production agenda in 1st SONA
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that the administration would raise production to counter food-price spikes and support purchasing power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement published by the implementing department with concrete policy direction.
contrary_evidence: The claim is a policy direction, not a delivery outcome.
Food-price pressure was partly inherited and global.

unresolved_gaps: No direct nuclear-command or crisis-use decision in 2022.
No external war or proxy-conflict record in 2022, so some conduct lenses are structurally thin.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for red-tagging and some police outcomes remains limited.
Election-year evidence is stronger on campaign behavior and information environment than on post-inauguration institutional change.
National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.

run_provenance.source_mix_note: Rich source metadata and chapter-specific reviewer exclusions were preserved during deterministic conversion.
